issues.legal_issue: A conviction for forgery cannot be sustained on an unacceptable accomplice account that lacks material corroboration connecting the accused to the alleged forgery.
material_facts: The conviction concerned pattas alleged to have been forged as valuable securities.
The approver was the principal witness linking the appellant to the alleged forgery, but the Court found his account unimpressive and not trustworthy.
The pattas bore the appellant’s own signatures, and the evidence did not reliably establish that the other purported signatures were forged.
The Court found no corroboration of the approver’s account in material particulars connecting the appellant with the forgery.
issues.conclusion: The conviction for forgery was unsustainable on the evidence and was quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 133 and 114 illustration (b) of the Evidence Act, an accomplice is competent to testify and a conviction on uncorroborated accomplice evidence is not legally invalid; however, the rule of prudence ordinarily requires corroboration in material particulars connecting the accused with the crime. The court must first assess the accomplice’s testimony on its own, and corroboration is unnecessary only where it is safe to dispense with it. For the forgery charge, Sections 463 and 467 of the Penal Code concern making a false document with the specified intent and punishment for forgery of a valuable security; Section 30 defines valuable security. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: appeal_from_forgery_conviction and conviction_depends_on_accomplice and approver_testimony_unacceptable and no_material_corroboration_connects_accused

predicates.appeal_from_forgery_conviction: The case is an appeal challenging a conviction for forgery.
predicates.conviction_depends_on_accomplice: The conviction linking the accused to the forgery depends on testimony from an accomplice.
predicates.approver_testimony_unacceptable: The court finds the accomplice’s account intrinsically unconvincing or untrustworthy.
predicates.no_material_corroboration_connects_accus: There is no reliable supporting evidence in material particulars connecting the accused to the alleged forgery.

issues.definition: When a forgery appeal depends on an accomplice whose account is unacceptable and lacks material corroboration connecting the accused, the forgery conviction is unsustainable.

issues.legal_issue: A conspiracy conviction cannot be sustained when the sole supporting accomplice account is unconvincing and uncorroborated, and the alleged acts in furtherance of the common criminal purpose have not been established.
material_facts: The only direct evidence of conspiracy was the approver’s testimony.
The Court had found the approver’s account concerning the alleged forgery unconvincing and did not accept it as reliable proof of the conspiracy.
The alleged acts said to have been done in furtherance of the conspiracy were not accepted by the Court as established criminal acts.
The approver’s account of the conspiracy was uncorroborated.
issues.conclusion: The conspiracy charge could not be sustained, and the appellant’s conviction was quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Conspiracy is generally proved by inference because direct independent evidence is seldom available, but the inference is ordinarily drawn from acts of the parties in pursuance of an apparent criminal purpose shared between them. An accomplice is competent to prove conspiracy, but the court applies the same caution concerning the reliability and corroboration of accomplice evidence. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: appeal_from_conspiracy_conviction and only_approver_evidence and approver_account_unconvincing and no_accepted_common_purpose_acts

predicates.appeal_from_conspiracy_conviction: The case is an appeal challenging a conviction for conspiracy.
predicates.only_approver_evidence: The accomplice’s testimony is the only direct evidence offered to prove the alleged conspiracy.
predicates.approver_account_unconvincing: The court finds the accomplice’s account of the alleged conspiracy unconvincing.
predicates.no_accepted_common_purpose_acts: The court does not accept as established acts showing pursuit of an apparent criminal purpose shared by the alleged conspirators.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a conspiracy conviction supported only by an unconvincing accomplice account and no accepted acts showing a shared criminal purpose, the conviction is unsustainable.

issues.legal_issue: A court must hear the appellant’s counsel before disposing of an application seeking additional evidence in a criminal appeal.
material_facts: During the criminal appeal, the appellant applied to recall a witness for further cross-examination and to have other witnesses examined or summoned.
The application was disposed of without giving the appellant’s counsel an opportunity to be heard in support of it.
The High Court judge dealt with the application after deciding the appeal.
issues.conclusion: Disposing of the application without hearing the appellant’s counsel was wrong and unjust, and the appellant had a right to a reasonable opportunity to be heard; the Court did not decide the merits of the request for additional evidence.
issues.legal_principle: A party seeking relief through an application in a criminal appeal must be afforded a reasonable opportunity to be heard in support of that application. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.criminal_appeal: The proceeding is a criminal appeal.
predicates.application_seeks_additional_evidence: A party applies to recall or summon witnesses to obtain additional evidence.
predicates.application_disposed_without_counsel_hea: The court disposes of that application without hearing the applicant’s counsel.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, disposing of an application for additional evidence without hearing the applicant’s counsel makes the disposal unjust.
